query: I'm 10 years from retirement. Should I start de-risking now and how aggressively?

recommendations.title: Initiate Gradual Glide Path to 60/40 Allocation
recommendations.summary: Begin de-risking by shifting from current 60/40 equity/fixed income split to a target 55/45 over the next 12 months, then gradually move to 60/40 (bonds/equity) by age 65.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: At 55 with 10 years to retirement, you're in the critical wealth preservation phase. Your current 60% equity exposure (55% in stocks/ETFs) is appropriate for early de-risking but should follow a systematic glide path. Given your $1.8M retirement goal and current $755K net worth, you need continued growth while reducing volatility. A gradual shift to 55/45 now, then 50/50 by age 60, and 40/60 by retirement balances growth needs with risk reduction. This approach reduces sequence-of-returns risk while maintaining sufficient equity exposure to reach your goal with additional savings of approximately $70K/year. Your stable income, low debt, and advanced experience support this measured approach rather than aggressive de-risking.
recommendations.suggested_action: Redirect new contributions to increase BND holdings; consider adding intermediate-term treasury ETFs (IEF) or target-date funds approaching 2035

recommendations.title: Add Inflation-Protected Securities and Dividend Aristocrats
recommendations.summary: Allocate 10-15% to TIPS and dividend-growth stocks to hedge inflation and generate reliable income as you approach retirement.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your portfolio lacks inflation protection, which is critical for a 10-year runway to retirement when inflation can significantly erode purchasing power. Your goal of $80-100K annual retirement income requires inflation-adjusted planning. Adding TIPS (via SCHP or TIP) provides real return guarantees. Additionally, your individual stock holdings (JNJ, UNH, PG, BRK.B) are excellent quality but represent only 15% of portfolio. Increasing exposure to dividend aristocrats with 25+ year histories of dividend growth provides both income generation training wheels and lower volatility than growth stocks. This positions you for eventual income generation while maintaining moderate growth. Allocate 10% to TIPS and increase dividend-growth stocks to 20% of equity allocation over next 18 months.
recommendations.suggested_action: Add 10% position in TIPS ETF (SCHP); increase dividend aristocrat allocation using VIG or NOBL ETFs

recommendations.title: Maintain Core Quality Holdings Through Retirement
recommendations.summary: Keep your high-quality core positions (JNJ, UNH, JPM, BRK.B, PG) as they provide stability, dividends, and defensive characteristics suitable for pre-retirement phase.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your individual stock selections demonstrate advanced investment acumen - all are industry leaders with strong balance sheets, consistent dividend growth, and lower volatility than broader market. JNJ and PG (consumer staples/healthcare) are defensive; UNH benefits from demographic tailwinds; JPM and BRK.B provide financial sector exposure with exceptional management. These holdings align perfectly with pre-retirement objectives: capital preservation, income generation, and inflation protection through pricing power. At 15% of portfolio, they're appropriately sized. These stocks should remain core holdings through retirement, potentially increasing to 20-25% as you reduce broader equity index exposure. Their combined dividend yield of 2-3% with growth potential provides income foundation. Do not sell these positions during de-risking; instead, reduce VTI exposure when rebalancing.
recommendations.suggested_action: Hold all positions; consider adding incrementally on market pullbacks of 10%+

recommendations.title: Implement Annual Rebalancing Calendar with Rising Cash Buffer
recommendations.summary: Establish systematic annual rebalancing and build cash reserves from 5% to 10% by retirement to cover 12-18 months of expenses and reduce forced selling risk.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Sequence-of-returns risk is your primary threat in the decade before retirement. Your current 5% cash ($42,500) covers approximately 4 months of expenses - insufficient for pre-retirement security. Build this to 10% ($85,000+ as portfolio grows) by retirement to cover 12-18 months of expenses, preventing forced asset sales during market downturns in early retirement. Implement annual rebalancing each January to systematically harvest gains, maintain target allocation, and increase bond/cash positions. This disciplined approach prevents emotional decisions during volatility and ensures gradual de-risking occurs on schedule. Set calendar reminders for annual reviews at age 56, 57, 58, etc., with predetermined allocation targets (55/45 now, 52/48 at 57, 50/50 at 60, 45/55 at 62, 40/60 at 65). This structured approach leverages your advanced experience while removing decision fatigue.
recommendations.suggested_action: Increase cash allocation to 7% immediately; target 10% by age 60; establish annual January rebalancing calendar
